atlas-ca.0084: CompTIA projects more than 414,000 tech jobs in the Toronto area in 2025, nearly 11% of its workforce against 6.8% for Canada, and puts Canada’s net tech employment at 1.45 million in 2024.
atlas-ca.0085: Reporting CompTIA’s Canadian data, a Vancouver technology news site (5 August 2025) gives tech employment of 414,000 in Toronto, 217,000 in Montréal, 150,000 in Vancouver, 69,000 in Calgary and 40,000 in Edmonton.
atlas-ca.0086: Statistics Canada’s Labour Force Survey for August 2026 puts unemployment at 6.4% with 21,173,000 people employed; for 15-to-24-year-olds it was 12.9%, against 14.3% a year earlier and a 2017–2019 average of 10.8%, and in the Toronto area it was 6.7%, down from a high of 9.0% in July 2025.
atlas-ca.0087: Statistics Canada’s income tables give average employment income in 2024 for full-year full-time workers of C$97,300 in the Toronto area, C$94,100 in Vancouver, C$94,000 in Ottawa–Gatineau, C$87,700 in Calgary and C$84,300 in Montréal, against C$85,500 for Canada; for all workers with employment income the Toronto average is C$68,100.
atlas-ca.0088: The Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation’s 2025 rental survey, republished by Statistics Canada, gives the average rent of a one-bedroom flat in purpose-built buildings of three units or more as C$1,807 in Vancouver, C$1,761 in Toronto, C$1,581 in Calgary, C$1,542 in Ottawa–Gatineau and C$1,131 in Montréal.
atlas-ca.0089: The University of Waterloo’s co-op calendar has employers hire for the fall term from May to August, for the winter term from September to December and for the spring term from January to April, in three matching cycles per term; for winter 2027 the matches fall on 9 October, 13 November and 27 November 2026.
atlas-ca.0090: CPABC says the fall is the main recruiting season for CPA training positions, with most activity from August to October, spring events typically run from March to June, and larger firms often hire about a year before the start.
atlas-ca.0091: The federal public service had 345,282 employees at the end of March 2026, against 357,965 a year earlier; applications fell nearly 30% to under 735,000 in 2025-26 and job ads fell almost 40%.
atlas-ca.0092: Federal bilingual posts carry a language profile of three letters (reading, writing, oral) at levels A, B or C, up to a maximum of CCC.
atlas-ca.0093: From 1 June 2025 Québec businesses with 25 to 49 employees must register with the Office québécois de la langue française and assess their use of French, as larger firms already had to; a law firm’s summary of the Charter of the French language.
atlas-ca.0094: Canada’s distinctive door is co-op: degrees that alternate study terms with paid work terms, so students graduate with a year or two of Canadian experience and often an offer from a former co-op employer. Employers ask for “Canadian experience”, and co-op is how students get it.
atlas-ca.0095: Since 1 January 2026 Ontario employers with 25 or more employees may not require Canadian experience in a public job posting, but professional licensing rules are exempt and a posting that does not ask for it still goes to the candidate who already has it.
atlas-ca.0097: Waterloo says more than 8,000 active employers recruit from its co-op pool and that over 24,000 full-time positions a year are posted on WaterlooWorks and filled by co-op students; co-op graduates earn more and land jobs that better match their field.
atlas-ca.0098: Hiring runs in three cycles per term, each with postings, interviews, student ranking of employers and a match date: for the winter 2027 term, cycle 1 matches on 9 October 2026, cycle 2 on 13 November and cycle 3 on 27 November, and direct offers start after the last match.
atlas-ca.0099: Campus recruiting for CPA training positions
atlas-ca.0100: Accounting firms and banks hire students for CPA training roles through regional campus recruitment frameworks. CPABC describes two seasons, with the fall as the main one (most activity August to October) and spring running March to June, and larger firms often hire about a year ahead.
atlas-ca.0101: Some firms follow the regional deadlines and others set their own, so each firm’s process has to be checked; the Big Four also cut staff and hired fewer graduates in 2023 and 2024.
atlas-ca.0103: The big banks run structured entry: RBC’s CPA Rotational Program lasts 30 months in internal audit and finance and recruits in the summer for a start in the autumn of the following year; Scotiabank’s CPA stream also lasts 30 months and starts in June.
atlas-ca.0104: RBC’s other graduate entries are a Capital Markets programme for undergraduate or master’s degree holders and a permanent Analyst programme; the pages read give no application dates, so postings have to be watched.
atlas-ca.0105: Federal public service student and graduate hiring
atlas-ca.0106: The Federal Student Work Experience Program (FSWEP) keeps an ongoing inventory open all year for more than 200 departments and agencies; managers pick matching applicants for a test or interview, and citizens and permanent residents get preference.
atlas-ca.0107: The door is narrowing: the federal public service fell from 357,965 employees in March 2025 to 345,282 in March 2026, applications fell nearly 30% to under 735,000 in 2025-26, and Budget 2025 aims to cut about 40,000 positions by April 2029, about half of recent cuts being casual, student or term roles.
atlas-ca.0108: Direct application through boards and employer sites
atlas-ca.0109: The Government of Canada Job Bank, TalentEgg (co-op, internship and entry-level roles), Eluta and Indeed are the boards university career offices name, with a warning that boards alone are not the most effective method and that company sites should be checked first. Experienced hires apply the same way.
atlas-ca.0110: Ontario postings from 1 January 2026 must state the pay or a range (no wider than $50,000, and not needed above $200,000), say whether AI screens applicants and whether a vacancy exists; an interviewed applicant must hear within 45 days whether a hiring decision has been made.
atlas-ca.0111: Informational interviews and referrals matter much as in the US, especially for newcomers without Canadian experience.
atlas-ca.0112: A career office says boards are not the most effective method on their own and advises asking people in your field which boards they use.
atlas-ca.0113: Youth unemployment (ages 15 to 24) was 12.9% in August 2026, against 14.3% a year earlier and an average of 10.8% in 2017–2019; the all-age rate was 6.4%.
atlas-ca.0114: Cuts are visible where graduates apply: the federal public service shed more than 12,600 jobs in a year, and PwC and Deloitte Canada cut staff in 2023 and 2024.
atlas-ca.0115: Co-op and campus cycles are set a term or a year ahead, so the hiring year that matters is the one before the start date, not the year of graduation.
atlas-ca.0116: The big banks hire graduates into rotational programmes: RBC runs a two-year leadership programme of four six-month rotations plus capital-markets and technology tracks; Scotiabank’s programmes include a CPA stream.
atlas-ca.0117: The Big Four recruit accounting students on campus for CPA training contracts, but PwC and Deloitte Canada cut staff in 2023 and 2024, and the firms hired fewer graduates.
atlas-ca.0118: A CPA Ontario programme such as RBC’s asks for a recognised degree of at least 120 credit hours with a minimum 70% average, the Knowledge Assessment or CPA qualifying courses, and registration with CPA Ontario before the start.
atlas-ca.0119: The federal route is FSWEP for students and, for bilingual posts, a second-language test late in the process; the Communications Security Establishment, one of the federal employers, takes only Canadian citizens.
atlas-ca.0120: Co-op is the door to software: Shopify takes 40% of its interns from Waterloo and likes to hire them full-time after their terms; the banks run technology new-graduate programmes too.
atlas-ca.0121: AI hiring runs through the three national institutes and their professors: more than 850 students from Vector-affiliated AI master’s programmes have been hired by Ontario firms, and Mila in Montreal and Amii in Edmonton place students with partner companies and banks.
atlas-ca.0122: The Communications Security Establishment runs student placements for full-time Canadian college and university students, in Ottawa or by telework; it asks to apply about eight months ahead, and the security clearance for students takes about six months.
atlas-ca.0123: Waterloo is the co-op reference: more than 8,000 active employers recruit from its pool, and Shopify takes 40% of its interns there. Western’s Ivey MSc reported an 85% offer rate for 2023/24 and a median base of C$75,000.
atlas-ca.0124: CPA recruitment in each region is organised by the schools and the provincial CPA body, so your school’s career office decides which firms you meet and when.
atlas-ca.0125: Employers host their own information and networking sessions, universities offer events through career services, and CPABC runs information sessions, webinars and career events every month. Waterloo employers can also host information sessions.
atlas-ca.0126: Co-op hiring has three cycles in each of three terms (fall, winter, spring); the CPA firms hire mainly in the fall, from August to October, and again in spring; the federal student inventory is open all year.
atlas-ca.0127: Bank and CPA entries accept a bachelor’s, a postgraduate diploma or a master’s: RBC Capital Markets takes undergraduate or master’s degree holders and Scotiabank’s CPA stream takes bachelor’s, diploma and master’s graduates. Ivey’s pre-experience master’s reported an 85% offer rate.
